explanation: Standard form gives P(x)=1/[x(x+1)] and Q(x)=ln(x)/(x-3). At x=0, x²Q(x) is not analytic, so the point is irregular singular. At x=2 both coefficients are analytic, so it is ordinary. At x=3, (x-3)P(x) and (x-3)²Q(x) are analytic, so it is regular singular. At x=-1 the real logarithm is undefined, so none of the supplied classifications is valid for the real equation. A local complex logarithm branch would instead make x=-1 regular singular; the problem does not specify this interpretation.
